steps.description: Compute false positive rates `fpr`, true positive rates `tpr`, and thresholds `thr` from `(yc_test, y_prob)` using `roc_curve`, then compute the area under that curve with `roc_auc = auc(fpr, tpr)`.
Pass `fpr`, `tpr`, and `roc_auc` to `RocCurveDisplay(...).plot()`, format `roc_auc` to 3 decimal places in the title, and call `plt.show()`.
Notice that `roc_curve` takes the continuous probabilities `y_prob` rather than the hard 0/1 predictions `y_pred` so it can evaluate `(fpr, tpr)` across all possible decision thresholds `thr`.

steps.answer: Building the ROC curve requires varying the decision threshold across continuous predicted probabilities `y_prob` to get a full sequence of `(fpr, tpr)` pairs. `y_pred` is already fixed at a single threshold.
